To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Deep reinforcement learning is a viable approach for learning to prove theorems in large knowledge bases, 2) the tf-idf based exploration mechanism is a simple and effective method for exploring large knowledge bases, and 3) the performance of the tf-idf mechanism is robust to a number of assumptions that are made in our implementation, including the choice of the underlying knowledge base and the choice of the exploration mechanism
(i) DeepHOL Zero can learn to reason in a large knowledge base without imitation and (ii) the tf-idf based lookup is a crucial component in the success of DeepHOL Zero.

(i) DeepHOL Zero outperforms provable baseline methods and (ii) the performance gain is due to a combination of the tf-idf lookup and the use of the full knowledge base as the source of potential premises.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to learn to explore a large space of premises in automated theorem proving without human guidance.
the problem of automated reasoning in the presence of large knowledge bases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is the first to learn from a large number of automatically generated proofs without human supervision.
we have demonstrated that a reinforcement learner can learn to explore premises without imitation and can approach the performance of a learner that uses both reinforcement learning and imitation.
DeepHOL Zero is a viable and competitive approach to learning to prove in the presence of large theories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to do automated reasoning with deep learning in the presence of large knowledge bases without learning from human proof.
we show that it is possible to learn how to reason in the presence of large knowledge bases without learning from human proof.
DeepHOL Zero learns how to reason in large theories from scratch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can train an automated theorem prover to reason in large knowledge bases without human proof examples.
it is possible to train a deep learning based theorem prover in the presence of many potential premises without learning human proofs.
